source.title: Landscape and training regimes in deep learning
source.authors: M. Geiger; Leonardo Petrini; M. Wyart

record.file_problem: Full review text supplied. The paper reviews cited work and reports its own empirical results; some results are shown in figures whose precise values are not given in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The review reports its own sweeps of network width and initialization scale, ensemble averaging, and comparisons of lazy and feature-learning regimes. These use different questions and methods from several listed versions but directly measure test error and generalization in the stated settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reviews numerous findings from prior work; cited results are not recorded as rows. Rows below cover its own reported experiments and measurements. General discussion of jamming, NTK limits, and invariants is not separately rowed unless the paper reports an outcome for it.
record.test_reason: The paper's new width sweeps test V2 in a different setting: two-hidden-layer fully connected networks on binary, PCA-reduced MNIST and CIFAR-10. Section 3 explicitly states that individual-network test error continues improving beyond the zero-training-loss threshold. The different architecture does not make this unrelated to V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors argue that passing the jamming threshold permits zero training loss, and explain continued individual-network improvement with width through diminishing initialization-induced fluctuations. Ensemble averaging largely removes this width dependence. They distinguish lazy and feature-learning regimes, review architecture-dependent performance differences, and leave the explanation of realistic image-learning performance unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Review article with new empirical phase-diagram measurements and reported experiments on fully connected networks and CNNs; it does not reproduce the original methods of the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Test-error behavior varies with width, initialization scale, ensemble averaging, architecture (fully connected versus CNN), and training regime (NTK versus feature learning).

fits_no_version.finding: Individual-network test error peaks near jamming, and ensemble averaging removes that peak.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization-dependent fluctuations produce a test-error peak near interpolation in these experiments. The peak itself is separate from V2's post-interpolation width claim.

fits_no_version.finding: The reviewed comparisons favor lazy training for many fully connected settings and feature learning for CNNs, with different learning-curve exponents.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relative performance of lazy and feature-learning regimes depends on architecture and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Reviewed stripe-model results connect weight alignment and compression of irrelevant dimensions to improved learning-curve exponents.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature learning can improve sample efficiency by reducing sensitivity to uninformative input directions.

record.problems: The paper is a review and many discussed findings are from cited work rather than the authors’ own experiments. The new empirical measurements use reduced binary datasets projected onto 10 or 30 principal components, small training sets, and a limited number of initialization samples. Several plotted results are not numerically transcribed in the text; CNN comparison details are limited in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately stated numeric outcome for the width sweep or the CNN/fully-connected dataset comparisons beyond the included qualitative findings. Prior-work results reviewed in Sections 1–5 and cited figures are excluded as not this paper’s own results.

untested.parts: No new paired experiment on fitting random labels and generalizing on natural labels; the random-label finding is cited.
The original one-hidden-layer ReLU setup and full classification tasks are not reproduced. These experiments use two hidden layers, binary labels, PCA-reduced inputs and 5000 training examples.
No new controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison, locality ablation, sparse-connection experiment or initialization-transfer test.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No batch-size comparison under controlled epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware perturbation measure ranked against generalization gaps. Hessian spectra and initialization fluctuations measure different properties.
No removal and retraining experiment based on example memorization.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is not an original source listed for V2. Its new Figures 4 and 6 provide relevant evidence despite its review format. Figures 9–11 and the stripe-model results are explicitly attributed to earlier publications; shared authorship does not make those new results here. Exact figure values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test fitting fixed random labels alongside natural labels.
The width sweep reports a peak and subsequent improvement, but it does not test the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10 without explicit regularization.
No controlled comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on the listed image datasets is reported.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers and SGD is reported.
No large-batch versus small-batch comparison is reported.
The paper does not test magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of the generalization gap.
No memorized-example removal experiment is reported.
